title: Mexico City Golf Experience: City, food and private-club golf in one trip

overview: A stay at Four Seasons Hotel Mexico City, on Paseo de la Reforma beside Chapultepec, with a round at El Coral, a public course, and visitor rounds at Madeiras and Bosque Real arranged in advance. Visitor access at the private clubs is not guaranteed and is usually easier on weekdays, so we place El Coral on the weekend. Green fees are charged separately and confirmed in your itinerary.
whyWeChoseIt: We selected Four Seasons because it is the Mexico City hotel golfers ask for first, its courtyard makes the city easy, and it lets us add a stay with weekend golf to a region where our other trips are weekday-only.
notIncluded: Caddie fees where the course requires them (confirmed in your itinerary)

gimReview: Our Mexico City trips were built around weekday access to private clubs. This one adds the city's best-known hotel and El Coral, a public course you can play on a Saturday, with the private clubs during the week when they admit visitors.
nonGolferFriendly: Yes: Chapultepec Park and Polanco nearby, the hotel's courtyard, spa and Zanaya restaurant, and the city's museums and dining.

overview: A design-led Nobu Hotel Los Cabos stay paired with Pacific-side golf. Diamante Dunes is a Davis Love III, Mark Love and Paul Cowley design (par 72, 7,160 yards). El Cardonal is Tiger Woods's first completed design and hosts the PGA TOUR's World Wide Technology Championship (par 72, 7,363 yards from the back tee). Solmar (Greg Norman, links-style, opened 2020, par 72, 7,240 yards); its par-3 17th (about 191 yards) plays to an island green. Oleada is added when outside-player availability is confirmed. Every private-course tee time must be confirmed before the trip is sold. Golf is booked separately from the hotel.
whyWeChoseIt: We selected Nobu Hotel Los Cabos for travelers who want a contemporary luxury hotel close to the Pacific-side golf corridor. Dunes and El Cardonal are the core reasons to travel; Solmar and Oleada add Pacific-side variety when access, operating status and tee times are confirmed.
notIncluded: Caddie fees where the course requires them (confirmed in your itinerary)
courseAccess: Diamante Dunes and El Cardonal are private clubs; tee times are arranged and confirmed by GOLF° IN MEXICO°. Solmar is open to the public. Oleada tee times are arranged and confirmed by GOLF° IN MEXICO°.
typicalDriveToCourses: 10 to 25 min to Solmar and Oleada (approximate); Diamante courses confirmed in your itinerary
gimReview: A stylish stay that happens to be close to Pacific-side golf. Nobu Hotel Los Cabos is a contemporary luxury hotel near the golf corridor, with the Diamante courses, Solmar and Oleada within reach. We recommend it for the hotel first and the golf second.
nonGolferFriendly: Yes: Esencia spa, an adults-only pool, the Nobu restaurant and excursions. The beach is not ideal for swimming.

overview: A private-residence group experience centered on Punta Mita's two Jack Nicklaus Signature courses. Pacífico (1999, par 72, 7,014 yards) has the optional par-3 3B, 'Tail of the Whale', on a natural island green. Bahía (2008, par 72, 7,035 yards) is #12 and #7, with five holes along the Pacific. We selected a qualifying residence because it keeps the group together and provides the access both courses require. Mandarina (Greg Norman) and Higuera are regional additions that need separate confirmation and longer transfers.
whyWeChoseIt: We selected a Punta Mita Rentals residence because it keeps groups together and provides the access framework needed for Pacífico and Bahía. Those two courses anchor the trip; Mandarina and Higuera are regional additions that bring more variety, with longer transfers.

nonGolferFriendly: Yes: private villa, in-home dining and the Punta Mita beach clubs.

title: Mayakoba: Championship golf in the Riviera Maya

courses.name: El Camaleón Mayakoba
courses.description: Greg Norman course through jungle, cenotes and mangrove-lined canals; former PGA TOUR venue and now LIV Golf's Mexico event.

courses.name: Gran Coyote
courses.description: Nick Price design through preserved jungle, with water hazards and bunkers close to the greens.

courses.name: PGA Riviera Maya
courses.specs: Robert Trent Jones II, par 72, 7,272 yds
courses.description: Robert Trent Jones II design on a former limestone quarry, with cenotes, jungle and mangroves in play.

courses.name: El Tinto
courses.description: Long Nick Price layout in preserved jungle with five lakes and 84 bunkers, formerly TPC Cancún.

overview: A refined Riviera Maya base at Alila Mayakoba with El Camaleón as the anchor round. Greg Norman's course (2006, par 72, 7,116 yards) runs through jungle, cenotes and mangrove-lined canals, hosted the PGA TOUR's Mayakoba Golf Classic from 2007 to 2022 and now hosts LIV Golf's Mexico event. We chose Alila because staying inside Mayakoba is the most natural pairing with El Camaleón, with a quiet-luxury and wellness profile. Gran Coyote, PGA Riviera Maya (Robert Trent Jones II, par 72, 7,272 yards) and El Tinto (Nick Price, par 72, 7,439 yards) complete the itinerary. Golf is booked separately unless the offer states otherwise.
whyWeChoseIt: We selected Alila because staying inside Mayakoba creates the most natural pairing with El Camaleón while delivering a quiet luxury and wellness profile. El Camaleón is the signature round; Gran Coyote, PGA Riviera Maya and El Tinto broaden the trip without requiring a hotel change.
notIncluded: Caddie fees where the course requires them (confirmed in your itinerary)
courseAccess: El Camaleón is open to resort guests and the public, with blackout dates around major events. Gran Coyote and El Tinto are open to the public. Access to PGA Riviera Maya is confirmed by GOLF° IN MEXICO°.
typicalDriveToCourses: 5 to 15 min to El Camaleón and Gran Coyote; 35 to 60 min to PGA Riviera Maya and El Tinto (approximate)
gimReview: El Camaleón is the reason to stay here: jungle, cenotes and mangroves on the course, and a quiet-luxury resort on the property for the rest of the day. The course hosted the PGA TOUR's Mayakoba Golf Classic from 2007 to 2022 and now hosts LIV Golf's Mexico event. Gran Coyote, PGA Riviera Maya and El Tinto can be added without changing hotels.
nonGolferFriendly: Yes: spa with temazcal, beach club, six restaurants and bars, and excursions.

title: San Miguel: #1 destination city, golf, wine and art
seoTitle: San Miguel de Allende Golf Trip

courses.name: Club de Golf Malanquín
courses.description: Tree-lined parkland course in San Miguel de Allende with kikuyu fairways, small lakes and streams.

courses.name: Ventanas de San Miguel
courses.specs: Nick Faldo with Schmidt-Curley, par 70, 7,141 yds
courses.description: Nick Faldo design above San Miguel de Allende with dramatic elevation change and long championship holes.

overview: A luxury city-and-golf escape that pairs San Miguel de Allende's hospitality and culture with two club rounds. Ventanas de San Miguel (Nick Faldo, par 70, 7,141 yards) sits at elevation with pronounced terrain movement, and Malanquín (par 72, 7,289 yards) is a tree-lined parkland course. We selected a luxury central hotel so guests can enjoy the city's dining, architecture and nightlife between rounds. Because both clubs need advance access coordination, the trip is designed around confirmed tee times rather than walk-up availability, and green fees are included only when stated in the final proposal.
whyWeChoseIt: We selected a luxury central hotel so guests can enjoy San Miguel's dining, architecture and nightlife between rounds. Malanquín and Ventanas provide two distinct local golf experiences, but both require advance access coordination; the product is therefore designed around confirmed tee times rather than walk-up availability.
notIncluded: Caddie fees where the course requires them (confirmed in your itinerary)
courseAccess: Malanquín is technically private but welcomes visitors, and a caddie is mandatory. Ventanas de San Miguel is open to the public, with member priority for tee times, and a caddie is mandatory.
gimReview: Two good courses and one of Mexico's best towns. Rosewood San Miguel de Allende puts you in the center for dining, architecture and nightlife between rounds, with confirmed tee times at Malanquín and Ventanas arranged by GOLF° IN MEXICO°. We think it is the best choice for a golf trip that is mostly a cultural getaway.
nonGolferFriendly: Yes: San Miguel's historic center is a destination in itself, with galleries, restaurants and shopping.
